txt: A bemused expression. "Oh, I don't think *you* should be expecting an apology from *him*."
But hold on, what's that? For a split second his hand lingers... as though gesturing towards a stone placed right next to the front door...
For a moment the man on the balcony seems almost vulnerable. Something moves in the depths of his feline eyes: compassion, and a hint of understanding.
He doesn't reply, gesturing 'no' with his cigarette. In the neighbouring windows you can see faint reflections of his silhouette, all from different angles.
He doesn't reply, gesturing 'no' with his cigarette. Under the dull and darkening sky the neighbouring windows stand silent.
He doesn't reply, gesturing 'no' with his cigarette. Under the grey sky snow continues to pile on the neighbouring window sills.
He doesn't reply, gesturing 'no' with his cigarette. Under the grey sky the neighbouring windows are streaked with rain.
He gives you a honeyed smile, before shaking off the cigarette ash.
He shrugs. "He has his ways. I don't need to know every detail of his life."
He sighs. "I had a friend over."
He sighs: "That he won't be there when times get tough, I guess."
He takes another drag of his cigarette before knitting his brows. "What friend?"
He takes another drag of his unfiltered cigarette and looks around. It's getting dark and the neighbouring windows have lit up one by one.

I would often go there / To the tiny church there / The smallest church in Saint-Saëns / Though it once was larger

How the rill may rest there / Down through the mist there / Toward the seven sisters / Toward those pale cliffs there

I would often stay there / In there tiny yard there / I have been so glad here / Looking forward to the past here

But now you are alone /None of this matters at all
The smoker starts laughing and leans back against the counter: "Sure thing, officer, what do you want to know next?"
You see a young man on a balcony nursing a cigarette. His eyes have been following you for a while.
[Leave] I'm done.

"*Everything* will be constantly shifting and moving under our rule, the future will belong to a circus of identities, just spinning around, surreal and unreal... You won't even know who you are anymore."
"*How* can a bar be out of vermouth?"
"*Obviously* I'm gonna quit some day."
"*Trash*?" The young man shakes his head in confusion.
"A bit too dramatic, don't you think?" He says it like it's an aesthetic question. "If you really must do it then I'd go with something else... some other substance."
"A visitor from the first world. He's not like you and me, gendarme." He smiles and his smile seems melancholic. "He can always return."
"Absolutely *wonderful*."
"Absolution? I don't know that brand, but I'm pretty sure you can get Astras at the Frittte."
"Admiring the atmosphere..." He smiles. "What about you, officer?"
"Ah... But for the better part of history it *has been* illegal."
"All *real* connections begin in the mind."
"Alright, but make it quick. Once I finish this cigarette I have to run."
"And I *really* need to finish this cigarette," he replies with a subtle smile.
"And if I may ask, gendarme, what is this *committee* about?" He takes a measured drag of his cigarette.
"Apologies, but this is my last one." He takes another drag and shivers.
"As though I don't have enough going on already."
"As you wish." He takes another drag.
"Aw, shoot." He bursts out laughing. "Why not?"

"Beautiful!" The smoker crawls up to you like an animal preparing to jump. "Beautiful, that's exactly what we're looking for! Who knows, maybe you *were* homo-sexual in the past, maybe all of that has been *repressed*..." He circles his hands around you.
"Beautiful," he replies, smiling. As he looks at you, something sparkles in his eyes.
"Beautiful," he says again. A nearby street lamp casts shadows on his chin, drawing out the slender cheekbones.

"Because instead of the traditional family unit we're going to have all this *razzamatazz*," he wiggles his hands, "and mysteries, of course, too -- mysteries of *sexual* nature, very esoteric. And disco music and drugs."
"Besides, I've got to run."
"Blend in where?" He raises his brows. "A carneval?"
"But do you also like the *razzle-dazzle* of gold? Do you like parties and discos and having fun under the vibrant lights of Saturday night?"

"But then again -- you're a cop, it definitely fits the genre." He looks at his hands folded on a table. "*I* fit the genre, we all do... moulded by fiction like we're characters in some bad novella."
"Bye-bye, gendarme."
"Can't do it with class? Don't do it at all."
"Convenient," he nods. "But what are you doing *here*, talking to me?"
"Could I get a refill here, please?"
"Deep down everyone is lonely."
"Do think about it, officer." He starts laughing and leans back against the counter.
"Don't even get me started on beauty..."
"Don't worry, we'll meet again." He gently rests his hand on your shoulder. "Come find me in the bar of the Whirling some evening."
"Even the rain feels nice." He leans over the railing and sticks out his hand to feel the rain.
"Friends, I told you. Sunday friends. Friends who like to get together from time to time."
"Gendarmerie! You found me." The young man on the balcony gives you a bright smile, before taking another drag from his cigarette.
"God, of *course* it is. My friend is always trying to convince me I need a little more responsibility..."
"Good luck with the investigation." He walks away.
"Good luck with the investigation."
"He has keys. And he likes the view..." He waves gently with his cigarette-holding hand. "To the sea, I mean."
"He might have mentioned something about making a tour of some historical sites up the coast... in an unofficial capacity, of course."
"He sounded vaguely Oranjese." He closes his eyes. "No, not vaguely, scratch that. He sounded *definitely* Oranjese."
"Hello-hello. So what brings you here?"
"Help you? No, sorry, gendarme..." He shakes his charming head. "I have to run."
"Hey, what's that noise down there?"
"Hi again, gendarme."
"Hi, gendarme. Another rendezvous." There he is again -- the smoker on the balcony! Right here in the Whirling-in-Rags.
"Hi-hi. So what brings you here?"
"Hmm... maybe you should figure it out, detective."
"Hmm?" He hums. "What about me, gendarme?"
"Hmm?" he hums honeyed.
"How cunning." He raises his brows and you're not sure whether he's mocking you or not. "I like men who take what they want."
"Human psychology is definitely lazy, don't you think?"
"I *knew* I should've quit..."
"I am sorry, but I really don't have the information you're looking for." His voice is soft and deliberate. With a flick of his wrist, he sends the cigarette butt sailing over the rail...
"I am. So are you. What brings you here?"
"I can *tell* that you finally got him down. Thank you -- it was quite a disturbing sight, even by Martinaise standards."
"I can't get involved in this..."
"I couldn't tell you," he says, exhaling a little puff of smoke. "We don't usually see much of the *gendarmerie* around here."
"I don't have clients, only friends."
"I don't want to be seen talking to the *gendarmerie*, if that's okay. I just want to finish my cigarette."
"I guess you will." He tips his head ever so slightly toward you.
"I have some good news for you. My Sunday friend is visiting me tonight. I told him about you and he'd like to say hello. Step in, he's already waiting." He nods towards door #28.
"I have to say that you do look like someone who might be part of *the underground*. You have that very distinctive 'I-can't-understand-what's-going-on-here' look."
"I see you've found yourself a little something from my wardrobe." He scans you. "Not bad, not bad at all. What brings you here?"
"I told you, he can be very useful. I guess that's the charm of powerful people."
"I'd even go so far as to say that the view is a little *too good*, my dear gendarme. Do you have an estimate of when the body will be taken away?"
"I'm not sure that's a good idea."
"I'm not throwing anything."
"I'm practically a shrink minus the diploma."
"In any case, I would *love* to help, but the thing is, I don't know *where* he is. We don't talk about everything, you see..." He gently taps the end of his cigarette with his forefinger.
"In any event, good luck with whatever it is you're up to."
"Is it now?" He starts laughing. "Well, enjoy it."
"Is it really that important?" he asks you, adjusting his shirt.
"It does feel like the end of the week. It's so magical, the white falling against the black..."
"It is -- on Sundays." He smiles.
"It was mine. My friends use it from time to time to visit me." As he looks at you, something sparkles in his eyes.
"It was my Sunday friend."
"It's been a week and now they show up?"
"Just look at it..." He gestures towards distant motorways, all leading to golden La Delta. "It's a beautiful night. Who's going to stay in on a night like this?"
"Just reporting back whatever I was telling him."
"Last week? I don't know, look..." He looks around the courtyard again. Old patio chairs and dead house plants litter the scene.
"Last week? I don't know, look..." He looks around the courtyard again. Rain patters on the window sills and dead house plants, too late to do them any good.
"Last week? I don't know, look..." He looks around the courtyard again. Snow blankets the old patio chairs and dead house plants, and all the neighbouring windows are black.
"Listen, I really have to go." With a flick of his wrist he sends the extinguished cigarette sailing over the rail.
"Mhmh, that's why I chose this place." He looks away, his cigarette end glowing in the dark. "Martinaise is special, isn't it?"
"Muscular. Handsome." He shrugs nonchalantly. "Strong. Like one of those military types."
"My Sunday friend is visiting me tonight. I told him about you and he'd like to say hello. Step in, he's already waiting." He nods towards door #28.
"My Sunday friend," he repeats, his smile even wider than before. "He's brilliant, everyone wants to meet my Sunday friend. You'll see."
"My name? My name is Martin Martinaise."
"No, I don't think it came up."
"No, I just like to look good." A light breeze pulls back a flap of shirt.
"No, for god's sake, I don't want you to cry!" He takes a quick step back and looks around, clearly disturbed.
"No, not you two." He gestures idly. "Some more *muscular* type."
"No, not you." He gestures idly. "Some more *muscular* type."
"No, of course not. Could you please lower your voice?" He scans the courtyard. It's silent like the bottom of a well, every sound captured and reflected back.
"No, we won't." He takes one last drag of his cigarette, before stubbing it out on the balcony.
"No." He exhales a grey trail of smoke. "I don't think I will. This is between the two of you, you see."
"No." He studies you from across the table.
"Not a clue. I'm not his agenda keeper, you see."
"Not everything that needs to be said, needs to be heard."
"Not looking for any trouble, officer..." he says in a quiet voice. Despite the cold, his shirt hangs unbuttoned on his frame.
"Nothing. That I didn't see anything."
"Now, if you'll excuse me, I really need to get going."
"Occasionally." He takes another drag, filling his lungs with nicotine. "Why?"
"Of course I've thought about quitting but... for what?"

"Oh we're ambitious, we want to destroy the last vestiges of meaning, the last things people in Revachol have to hold on to, the true symbols of security -- the meaning of man and woman, mother and father, their marriage."
"Oh, a *committee*." He smiles. "How interesting..."
"Oh, a big *secret* committee. I understand perfectly..." His mouth forms a half smile.
"Oh, he'll be *devastated* to hear that, I'm sure..." He smiles.
"Oh, it's a *pleasure* group... a sub-rosa pleasure group congregating in cellars under the cover of night... Saturday night, sometimes even *Friday* night!"
"Oh, let me think..." He turns his eyes upward in recollection. "He had an accent. He sounded like one of those mercenaries."
"Oh, yes... let's see. He knocked on my door a few days after the lynching. I think he was going through the entire building, asking questions."
"Oh..." He waves lazily with his cigarette. "You already asked me that, didn't you?"
"Okay, *you* tell me this doesn't taste like shit..."
"Or Thursday night! Sometimes the congregating doesn't even end, it carries on into our daily life..." He lowers his voice conspiratorially and looks around.
"Or is it just money, I don't know..." He stares at the bar.

"Or the true symbols of security, mother and father and their everlasting marriage... *Everything* will be constantly shifting and moving under our rule, the future will belong to a *circus* of identities, just spinning around, surreal and unreal..."
"Really?" He straightens up, curious. "Well, I look forward to that!" He raises a glass to you.
"Scary how many people don't have *anyone* to talk to."
"So much for a quiet smoke."
"So tell me, are you here to make things *right* again?"
"Sorry, I don't have time for this. I just want to finish my cigarette and be gone."
"Sounds like a bore, frankly." He takes a drag of his cigarette. "All the fun stuff's down here..."
"Sure. Anything else on your mind?" His lazy eyes stroll over your face.
"Take care, alright?" he says with another disarming smile, before slipping off into the night.
"Thank you."
"That's nice, but I don't have anything to tell you. It's my friend you're looking for, not me."
"The *homo-sexual underground*?" The smoker sits up immediately, his eyes wide with amused surprise; a honeyed smile lingers on his lips.
"Then I have some good news for you..." His eyes narrow. A nearby street lamp casts shadows on his chin, drawing out the slender cheekbones.
"There won't *be* a next time." He takes a last drag of his cigarette, before stubbing it out in the balcony snow. "I really need to get going."
"There's no trouble, I'm just speaking in a *lowered voice*," he says sotto voce.
"There's only one problem: I don't think he wants to talk with *you*."
"To his opportunities in Occident, Sur-la-Clef. Still..." He breathes in and keeps his lungs filled for a moment, before letting it out. "His coming and going brings some life to the village."
"To the city." He gestures idly towards distant motorways. "It's a beautiful night."
"Trust me, I'm *not* a team player," he says with a honeyed smile.
"Trust me, you do."
"We are going to *change* the family unit with all this razzamatazz and finger-dancing," he wiggles his hands, "and with mysteries, of course, the mysteries are also of sexual nature, very esoteric."
"We'll talk," the smoker assures you, brushing his hand through the hair. "Just not tonight."
"Well, I *am* one of them, one of this *sub-rosa pleasure group* congregating in cellars under the cover of night... Saturday night, sometimes even *Friday* night!"
"Well, here's to you!" He raises a glass, before taking a sip of his drink, froth grazing his mouth.
"Why not? Don't you want to hear about how we want to destroy the last vestiges of meaning, the last things people in Revachol have to hold on to, the meaning of man and woman?"
"Why shouldn't he?"
"Why yes I am, officer. Why, do you want to *investigate*?"
"Yeah, it does feel like the end of the week. Such gentle weather..."
"Yes, but he was speaking to someone on his earpiece."
"Yes, we listen to a lot of disco. Some say we *engineered* disco to spread our vision of a vertiginous, ever-changing society, where all there is a razzle-dazzle of gold!"
"Yes, yes, I'm very attractive. Great, thank you."
"Yes, you know those tiny speaker-microphones that fancy security guards sometimes wear."
"Yes." He nods. "I think that would be prudent..."
"Yes?" A handsome young man hums with a cigarette in his hand. "Are you looking for me, gendarme?"
"You can keep it, I don't mind. I can appreciate beauty when I see it."
"You can't just get into it, you have to be born into it -- one is either already *in* the homo-sexual movement or forever excluded from it."
"You did?" A small smile adorns his face. "And how did you like him?"
"You won't even know who you are anymore."
"You're right, it's horrible for the skin. Very ageing." He takes another drag, before shaking off the ash.
